description:
🚀 VYOM-6 | NASA SPACE APPS CHALLENGE

Six minds. One mission. Beyond infinity.

We are VYOM 6, a team of curious and passionate individuals excited to explore the world of space, science, and technology through the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

We believe that great ideas come from collaboration, creativity, and the courage to learn something new. As aspiring innovators, we are eager to work with NASA's open data to develop meaningful solutions to real-world challenges.
summary:
C65 Interplanetary Habitability Exploration (Stage 1) is a browser-based 3D space exploration game built with Three.js. The player explores five planets, with C65 as the final world, to find which ones could support life.

Players choose a planet, pick one of four candidate landing sites, and drive a first-person rover across the surface. They analyse the terrain and collect samples of identified elements. Each sample weighs 3 g and the rover carries up to 3000 g.

An onboard analysis laboratory shows laser spectrum readings (measured vs. reference lines), environment traces, and nanoscale microscope views. Every planet and site receives a simulated habitability index out of 100, based on factors such as pressure, radiation and accessible water. The two highest-scoring planets are shortlisted as habitable.

In the final step, the player sends Sachari bacteria to one of the two shortlisted planets. The bacteria must survive on only one of them, judged by simulated survival requirements and a cyanobacteria oxygen indicator.

The game turns planetary science into a hands-on mission where data, not guesses, decides where life could survive.

All values are simulated mission data. The game measures environmental habitability only, not real biological survival or human habitation.

Tech: a single HTML file that runs in any browser with no installation.
